title: What is known about 1RB1RF_1RC1LC_1LD0LE_---1LE_1RF0LB_0RA1RE
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1RF_1RC1LC_1LD0LE_---1LE_1RF0LB_0RA1RE.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. Sweeps back and forth, rewriting period-5 words (00101, 10110 and their phases) and runs of 1s on every sweep; the tape is a soup of these pieces; a halt needs a leftward sweep to meet 0 0 1 just before a 1. Lean proves the sweep rules over the background words and the only local pattern that leads to a halt; no halt in 109 steps.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D0); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 49,297 cells have been visited and 30,020 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: sqrt/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.451). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512).

claims.title: The sweeps cross the background words whole
claims.text: 12 shift rules: for every n and every surrounding tape, a sweep in the stated state crosses n copies of a background word and leaves n copies of its partner, in the stated number of steps (for example L F> (00101)^n R ⟶ L (10101)^n F> R).

claims.title: The only way to a halt
claims.text: The machine halts only when D reads a 0, and the only way there is E reading a 1 with 0 0 1 just left of it (E, B and C step left and D meets the second 0.

claims.title: Same table as its twin
claims.text: This is the table of 1RB1LB_1LC0LD_---1LD_1RE0LA_0RF1RD_1RA1RE with the states renamed (A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→F, F→A); this machine starts in the state that one calls F. The two runs from blank tape are different (no common configuration at the left end in their first 300,000 steps), but they use the same sweeps, words and halting pattern, and every rule there holds here after renaming.

claims.title: What the tape looks like
claims.text: Seen at the left end (after a leftward sweep) the tape is a soup of runs 14 to 19, pieces 0 0 1 0 1 0 (01)3 and blocks (00101)k; seen at the right end (after a rightward sweep) it is blocks (10110)k, (01101)k, (10101)k, (101)k. Unlike the other machines of this group there is no long clean zone: the whole tape stays irregular.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not known. The shallow near miss (D on a 1 with 1 0 1 on its left) happens tens of millions of times, so the safety comes from the order of pieces, not from a rare event. No invariant is known.

claims.text: The same table as 1RB1LB_1LC0LD_---1LD_1RE0LA_0RF1RD_1RA1RE up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. explainer.lede: Nobody knows yet. Sweeps back and forth, rewriting period-5 words (00101, 10110 and their phases) and runs of 1s on every sweep; the tape is a soup of these pieces; a halt needs a leftward sweep to meet 0 0 1 just before a 1. This page runs the real machine, explains its sweeps and the words they rewrite, and lists what is proved.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 49,297 cells visited.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.451). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.512).
After 109 steps the tape spans 49,297 cells (12,768 left of the start, 22,030 right), with a density of 1s of 0.609.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Sweeps that rewrite a periodic tape
html: The head sweeps right (F, A, E) and left (B, C, D, E), turning where the local pattern sends it back. The pieces the sweeps cross whole are period-5 words and 01, 10: rightward, F turns 00101 into 10101 and 01001 into 01101, A turns 10010 into 11010, and both cross 01, 10 unchanged; leftward, C, B and E take the period-5 words back, and D, E fill 01, 10 to 11.

Seen at the left end (after a leftward sweep) the tape is a soup of runs 14 to 19, pieces 0 0 1 0 1 0 (01)3 and blocks (00101)k; seen at the right end (after a rightward sweep) it is blocks (10110)k, (01101)k, (10101)k, (101)k. Unlike the other machines of this group there is no long clean zone: the whole tape stays irregular.

sections.heading: What one sweep does to the words it crosses
html: A shift rule says that a sweep crosses any number n of copies of a word in one state and leaves n copies of another word behind. These are proved in Lean for every n and every tape around them (lean/Rules.lean); S> is the head in state S on the next cell, L and R the rest of the tape.

sections.heading: The one pattern that halts, and why it has not appeared
html: The machine halts only when D reads a 0, and Lean proves that the only way there is E reading a 1 with 0 0 1 just left of it (E, B and C step left and D meets the second 0; halt_needs_pattern, lean/Halt.lean). So a leftward sweep must reach 0 0 1 1 in E. Runs of three or more 0s do appear inside the tape for a moment (about 31,000 times in 2·108 steps), but never in that position.
The shallow near miss (D on a 1 with 1 0 1 on its left) happens tens of millions of times, so the safety comes from the order of pieces, not from a rare event. No invariant is known.
Next step. Find the block structure of the soup (which words occur between which separators) and the map of one round trip on blocks.

The two runs from blank tape are different (no common configuration at the left end in their first 300,000 steps), but they use the same sweeps, words and halting pattern, and every rule there holds here after renaming.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.
